correctness.rationale: Directed weighted matrix-tree theorem gives a polynomial degree enumerator and an independent-categorical representation. Its exact covariance is a sum of nonpositive one-hot covariances. Strict convexity/superadditivity identifies unique all-host minimum; independent binomial and categorical fluctuations yield the sharp correlation rate. Standard-library verifier checked 40 configurations, 102778 trees, 6834 complete distribution coefficients and 646 pair-covariance comparisons. Finite enumeration corroborates but does not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: Classical multivariate degree generating functions are acknowledged as covered and not claimed new. Claimed new contribution is the universal sharp optimization of two-degree covariance across every multipartite host composition and marked vertex pair, unique K_{1,1,N-2} minimizer, and asymptotic near-perfect anticorrelation rate. Search and inspected primary available material did not establish direct prior coverage, subject to 1994 full-text priority risk.

value.rationale: Uniform spanning-tree degree dependence is a natural probability invariant. The exact all-composition extremal problem has a uniquely characterized extremal host and dramatic order-N covariance versus zero covariance for bipartite cross-part pairs; the correlation reaches -1 at sharp N^-2 rate. These are structural distinctions relevant to stochastic network baselines, not a small arbitrary finite table or renaming of an existing invariant.
